text:
alex: Quick ping — opened a TF change to wire KMS for secrets-service (IRSA). Can someone eyeball the key_policy vs aws_kms_grant bits? Plan looks ok but not 100% sure about the grantee principal we should use. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482 :eyes:
priya: can you paste the relevant TF snippet here? easier to review inline
alex: sure, excerpt below:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "secrets_sa_role" {
  name = "secrets-service-irsa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "secrets" {
  description = "CMK for secrets-service"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "secrets_service" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.secrets.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.secrets_sa_role.arn
  operations = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```
notes: data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa includes the OIDC condition for `sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` for the k8s SA.
ben: two quick things: (1) `grantee_principal` should be the role ARN — that part is fine. (2) Grants are ephemeral from AWS semantics (and can be lost on key rotation/replication edge cases). You still need the key policy to allow the role principal long-term.
emily: agree with ben. We usually add an explicit key policy statement like:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowSecretsServiceRole",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/secrets-service-irsa" },
  "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
and keep the terraform `aws_kms_grant` for rotation/short-lived agents.
alex: thanks — should we put the role ARN directly in the key policy (hardcoded account id) or reference the TF role resource? concerned about drift across envs (staging/prod).
priya: reference the TF role resource in the key policy when possible, e.g. using `${aws_iam_role.secrets_sa_role.arn}` in the policy document. For multi-account deploys, we render different key policies per env (we have a module pattern for that).
infra-bot: terraform plan: 
+ aws_kms_key.secrets
+ aws_iam_role.secrets_sa_role
+ aws_kms_grant.secrets_service
(see PR for full diff)
ben: one more gotcha — if you plan to let other AWS services call KMS on behalf of the role (eg EC2 in another account) consider adding `kms:ViaService` condition or explicitly add the service principal in the policy. Not necessary for pure IRSA -> role flow.
alex: sweet. I'll update the key policy to reference the TF role arn and keep the grant for now. Will push a follow-up commit and tag you both for review. Thanks! :pray:
